text: Today, April 5th, 2026, at 8:30 AM, I went to have blood drawn and told the nurse I wanted it done in one go. The nurse said, "Let me check your veins first," and then wrapped a tourniquet around my forearm at the elbow crease. I asked if she was going to draw blood there, saying it's hard to find a vein (I've had blood drawn many times in various locations, and almost every nurse always uses the back of my hand). But she insisted on doing it there. I stayed silent. She then started probing and pushing the needle further in, unsure if she'd reached bone or tendon, which was incredibly painful. I screamed loudly in the clinic. She even had the nerve to ask if it hurt, saying she'd found a vein but only got a little blood, so she needed to move to another spot. I told her to stop. If she had listened to the patient instead of being so arrogant, it would have been much better. I've had blood drawn many times and seen nurses do this repeatedly, but I've never cried before. This time, it was too much. I know it's difficult to find a vein in my case, but nurses should listen to the patient, the one experiencing the pain.
